--- title: "[Graph.select_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select nodes using a predicate function. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19398-L19501){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.select_nodes(predicate) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Select nodes by predicate](/assets/graphs/select-nodes.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Six nodes A to F, each with a badge giving its w attribute (3, 8, 6, 2, 9, 4). After selecting with the predicate w greater than 5, nodes B, C, and E, whose values are 8, 6, and 9, are selected and drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} Calls a user-supplied function once for every node and adds the nodes for which it returns `True` to the current node selection. This is the most flexible way to build a selection: any rule that can be expressed in Python over a node's ID, label, or attributes can be used. A node selection is the input to the graph's "with selection" (`*_ws`) methods, so a typical workflow is select -> act: - tag or update a subset of nodes with `set_node_attrs_ws()` or `mutate_node_attrs_ws()` - inspect a subset as a table with `get_node_df_ws()` - prune nodes with `delete_nodes_ws()` or keep only them with `transform_to_subgraph_ws()` - use the nodes as a starting point for `trav_out()`, `trav_in()`, or `trav_both()` Selection is cumulative: matching nodes are added to whatever is already selected, and nothing is deselected. Call `clear_selection()` first to start fresh, or combine predicates in one function for AND/OR logic. The predicate runs in Python for every node, so on very large graphs the specialized selectors (e.g., `select_nodes_by_degree()`) are faster. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [predicate]{.doc-parameter-name} : A callable that receives a `Node` object and returns a `bool`. The `Node` exposes `id` (the integer node ID), `label` (the string label, or `None`), and `attributes` (a dict of the node's attributes, or `None` if the node has no attributes). Nodes for which the callable returns `True` are selected. The return value must be an actual `bool`: returning `None`, an integer, or another truthy object raises `TypeError`. Guard attribute access accordingly, e.g., `n.attributes is not None and ...` or `bool(...)`. Any exception raised by the predicate propagates, and nodes already visited at that point may remain selected. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the predicate returns something other than a `bool`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The predicate receives each node's `Node` object, so any of its properties -- `id`, `label`, or `attributes` -- can drive the filter. Here, only "hub"-typed nodes pass, and those are the nodes with IDs `1` and `3`: ::: {#da83e724 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A", type="hub", score=10) .add_node(label="B", type="leaf", score=5) .add_node(label="C", type="hub", score=8) .select_nodes(lambda n: n.attributes.get("type") == "hub") ) sorted(graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 3] ``` ::: ::: Filtering on `n.id` instead selects by internal node ID -- useful when IDs carry meaning, such as being assigned in a known order. Clearing first ensures the earlier selection doesn't carry over: ::: {#13d619ad .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.clear_selection() graph.select_nodes(lambda n: n.id >= 2) sorted(graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [2, 3] ``` ::: ::: When some nodes have no attributes, `n.attributes` is `None`, so guard the lookup. The selection then feeds a `*_ws` method -- here only "B", the one node with a score above `5`, gets the new `flag` attribute: ::: {#2562f945 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes([("A", {"score": 3}), ("B", {"score": 9}), "C"]) .select_nodes(lambda n: n.attributes is not None and n.attributes.get("score", 0) > 5) .set_node_attrs_ws(flag=True) ) graph.get_node_df().select("label", "score", "flag") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
